articles.title: US warns of rising illnesses in Cuba amid worsening water, power crisis; embassy issues health alert
articles.description: The US Embassy in Havana has raised alarms about rising intestinal illnesses in Cuba, attributing them to the deteriorating water and electricity systems on the island. Ongoing restrictions on fuel shipments from the US have intensified these power outages and sanitation issues. Both locals and visitors are advised to exercise caution regarding food safety and refrigeration practices. UN experts caution that these sanctions may exacerbate a larger public health emergency.

articles.title: US man duct-taped to seat after attacking passenger mid-flight, racial abuse
articles.description: An American Airlines flight traveling from Dallas to Newark had to make an unexpected stop in Baltimore due to a disruptive passenger. The individual reportedly attacked another traveler and directed racial insults toward a flight attendant. Thanks to the quick actions of retired law enforcement officer Juan Mejia and a vigilant flight attendant, the passenger was subdued using zip ties and duct tape for safety.

articles.title: Tesla’s wheel-free Cybercabs face US safety probe just a day after launch
articles.description: The US safety regulator is conducting an investigation into Tesla's innovative taxis that operate without a steering wheel. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is assessing whether these vehicles adhere to federal safety regulations. Following their launch in Austin, Texas, on Thursday, the agency plans to examine Tesla's self-certification process. This investigation echoes previous scrutiny experienced by competitor Zoox.

articles.title: Trump team quietly closed probe into businessman eyed by US to broker Venezuela oil deal
articles.description: The Trump administration sought Alejandro Betancourt's help for a major US oil deal with Venezuela. Federal prosecutors recently closed their investigation into Betancourt after administration officials intervened. Betancourt was investigated as part of a probe into alleged embezzlement and laundering from PDVSA. His position shifted as the administration sought a larger role for US companies in Venezuela's oil industry.

articles.title: Five Indiana engineering students built a 12-hour wearable that helps visually impaired users detect obstacles beyond a cane or guide dog
articles.description: Rose-Hulman students have developed a remarkable wearable device tailored for visually impaired individuals. This innovative headgear employs advanced sensors to identify surrounding obstacles, providing users with haptic feedback. With a remarkable twelve-hour battery life on a single charge, this device empowers users with greater independence. The project's goal is to enhance the day-to-day experiences of those with vision impairments.

articles.title: 'Mirzapur: The Movie' scores Rs 29 crore haul at box office
articles.description: Mirzapur: The Movie has achieved a significant opening day collection of Rs 24.75 crore net. This impressive debut places it as the fourth-highest opening day grosser for Hindi films in 2026. The film garnered substantial earnings from its Hindi release and a smaller contribution from its Telugu version. Occupancy rates increased throughout the day, indicating growing audience interest in the movie.

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s sister talks about how the family is dealing with everything
articles.description: Stella Parton has opened up about the profound grief her family is experiencing after the loss of Dolly Parton. She expressed her heartfelt appreciation for the support from close friends and family while highlighting the often harsh and thoughtless comments from outsiders. Stella called for greater compassion and understanding in our interactions and urged everyone to honor Dolly by embodying her spirit of respect and kindness during these trying times.
